items.title: Wolfenstein 3 Officially in Production, Confirms Xbox CEO
points: On the eve of Xbox’s 25th Anniversary on November 15, 2026, CEO Asha Sharma is announcing multiple updates to consoles, games, and upcoming titles, including Wolfenstein 3.
Following yesterday’s Xbox Playback recap announcement, the CEO has now confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production.
According to CEO Asha Sharma on X, MachineGames is officially working on the next Wolfenstein game, titled Wolfenstein 3, as confirmed in her post on November 13, 2026.
She attached a photo of the game’s script titled “Chapter 01-Nazitraz” featuring the iconic series main character, BJ Blazkowicz, and a handful of supporting characters.

MachineGames followed up the Xbox CEO’s tweet with another post including the same script alongside an image of two returning actors: Brian Bloom, the voice and mo-cap for BJ Blazkowicz, and Debra Wilson, who did the mo-cap and voice acting for Grace…
Most players expected the publisher to unveil Wolfenstein 3 at Xbox Games Showcase 2026, but better late than never.

items.title: Delhi reel under ‘severe’ level air pollution
points: Vehicles ply along a flyover shrouded in a thick layer of smog and haze as air quality deteriorates, in New Delhi.
File | Photo Credit: ANI The overall air quality of Delhi worsened to “severe” category on Friday (November 13, 2026) morning, according to official data.

Ballabgarh in Haryana also witnessed “severe” air pollution, while many other cities and towns in north India, including Noida, Gurugram, Faridabad witnessed “very poor” air quality, on Friday morning.
The 24-hour average overall Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 403 (severe) at 9 a.m. on Friday, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.
The overall air quality of Delhi is expected to be in the “severe’” category till Friday night, as per the Central government’s ‘Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi’.

items.title: Keralam to bring in athlete-centric sports bill: Minister Janeesh
points: Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam will overhaul its existing sports laws and introduce a comprehensive, athlete-centric sports bill to bring about reforms in the state's sports sector, Minister O J Janeesh has said.

The proposed legislation aims to address coordination gaps arising from the separate functioning of the State Sports Council and the Sports Directorate and make the sports sector more professional, he said.

The sports minister was speaking after inaugurating a function here on Thursday to distribute cash awards and honour sportspersons who won medals in national and international competitions during 2019-20.
The programme was organised by the State Sports Council at the Durbar Hall of the Secretariat here, according to an official statement.
The cash award for Asian Games gold medallists had been increased from ₹20 lakh to ₹50 lakh, while silver and bronze medallists were given ₹20 lakh and ₹10 lakh, respectively, he said.
Coaches were also provided ₹5 lakh, while sportspersons participating in the competitions received ₹one lakh each as travel assistance, he said.

items.title: Indore still on top in cleanliness survey, let score sheet be released, says mayor
points: Indore mayor Pushyamitra Bhargava has maintained that the city remains at the top of India's cleanliness rankings, challenging critics to wait for the detailed scorecard of the Centre's Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26.

Speaking to news agency Press Trust of India (PTI), Bhargava claimed that Indore had secured the highest marks in the National Clean City category, despite not figuring among the top three winners announced on Wednesday.
President Droupadi Murmu conferred the awards, marking the 10th edition of the survey, at a ceremony at Vigyan Bhavan in New Delhi.
Under the survey's rules, the Super Swachh League comprises cities that finished among the top three in their population categories in at least three of the 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024 editions.
League cities are assessed on additional indicators rather than ranked against one another and must score at least 85% to retain their position.
Ahmedabad, which won the 2024-25 survey, topped the newly introduced Swachh Shehar Jodi category with its partner town Sanand.

items.title: Man arrested for stabbing nephew for refusing to bring liquor from market in Gurugram
points: Gurugram police arrested a 35-year-old man for stabbing his nephew with a pair of scissors, leaving him injured after an argument over bringing liquor from the market in Sector-28.
The suspect, identified as Raju, is a resident of Chakarpur in Sector-28 and lived with his elder brother and nephew in a rented accommodation.
According to the police, he allegedly stabbed his nephew on the head and face around 1.30am on Wednesday after an argument over ordering liquor.
As per police, Raju was addicted to alcohol and was drinking liquor on Tuesday night when he had asked his nephew to fetch him more liquor from the market.
Gurugram police's public relations officer (PRO) Sandeep Turan said the victim refused to comply with Raju, resulting in a heated argument.

On complaint of the suspect’s brother, an FIR was registered against him under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita at DLF police station in Sector-29 on Wednesday, after which the suspect was traced and arrested.

items.title: Dead Fish In Yamuna Raise Political Stink, AAP And BJP Spar
points: Dead fish seen floating in the Yamuna have triggered a political war of words between the ruling BJP and the opposition Aam Aadmi Party (AAP).
Several social media users posted visuals of dead fish in the Yamuna ahead of the Chhath Puja festival along the Sonia Vihar stretch of the river in the Capital.
The sightings came just a day after the official launch of Delhi's first recreational river cruise service, the Namo Yamuna River Safari.
The incident has triggered a political row, with Delhi Environment Minister Parvesh Verma alleging that the dead fish were deliberately dumped into the river to discredit the government.

The Opposition AAP questioned, "If this water is not safe for fish, is it safe for humans?" Parvesh Verma alleged that some people were deliberately dumping dead fish adding that an FIR has been filed.
Read | Delhi Gets Its First Electric Cruise On Yamuna: Rs 500 Ticket, 40-Minute Ride This is the second incident of mass fish deaths in the Yamuna in one month.

items.title: 2027 Tata Nexon Spied – New Exteriors, Interiors, Wheels
points: Tata is working on the new-gen Nexon (codenamed Garud), which is expected to be launched in 2027.
Latest spy shots from Maharashtra offer a glimpse of the SUV’s road presence, exterior profile and interior.
With competition intensifying in the sub-4-metre segment, new Nexon is expected to get comprehensive updates.
Higher trims of new-gen Nexon could also get 18-inch alloy wheels as previous spy shots were spied testing with 18-inch alloys from Curvv.
New Nexon is expected to continue with the 1.2-litre turbo petrol engine.
This generates 120 PS and 170 Nm of torque.
Current Nexon is also available with a 1.5-litre Revotorq turbo diesel engine, which could be replaced with the new Kryojet turbo-diesel engine used with Sierra.
The latter has a slightly higher state of tune and a superior 6-Speed Torque Converter (AT) gearbox.

items.title: Tea Board panel recommends minimum sustainable price for tea; industry associations welcome move
points: A 10-member committee constituted by the Tea Board of India has recommended the introduction of a Minimum Sustainable Price (MSP) for tea, marking an important step towards addressing the widening gap between production costs and market realisations in the…

Several tea industry associations welcomed the move and emphasised the need for a sustainable pricing framework to ensure remunerative returns for tea producers and protect the interests of small tea growers and secure the long-term viability of the sector.

The Indian Tea Association (ITA), Tea Association of India (TAI), United Planters' Association of Southern India (UPASI), Confederation of Indian Small Tea Growers Associations (CISTA) and Federation of Indian Tea Manufacturers Association (FITMA) were…

According to a statement by the industry associations, tea prices have registered a marginal compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 2 to 3 per cent over the years, compared with an estimated CAGR of 10 to 14 per cent in input costs.

items.title: Three stocks that pass the value investing test
points: ‘The stock market is a device for transferring money from the impatient to the patient.' : Warren Buffett The stock market is not a place for speculators and gamblers.
So, it should be no surprise to hear the old stock market saying that more than 90% of traders lose money in the long term.
We would go further and say that most of the remaining 10% don't make enough for a good lifestyle.
In this editorial, we explain the steps to apply the principles of value investing and highlight three stocks from Equitymaster’s Stock Screener: Top Value Stocks in India.
The idea behind value investing is to buy stocks trading at a significant discount to their intrinsic value, usually more than 20%, i.e. , when there is a big margin of safety.
So, if the estimated intrinsic value is ₹100 per share, value investors will buy it only if the stock is trading below ₹80.

points: Azad Samaj Party (Kanshiram) chief Chandra Shekhar Azad has invited the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) to join his party’s newly formed Samajik Parivartan Morcha alliance with Asaduddin Owaisi’s All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul…
He said more parties will be given space in the bloc, and the priority is to prevent the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) from returning to power for a third consecutive term.
Azad’s party and the AIMIM contested the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections separately and failed to win a seat.
AIMIM contested 95 seats and secured 0.49% of the votes.
The Azad Samaj Party (Kanshiram) contested over 100 seats and polled around 0.13% of the votes.
The SP contested the 2022 assembly elections in an alliance with the Rashtriya Lok Dal, the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party, Apna Dal (Kamerawadi), Mahan Dal and the Janvadi Socialist Party.
He referred to his victory from Nagina in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, where he defeated the BJP candidate by 151,473 votes.

items.title: India bond selloff may continue as Treasury rout, fresh debt sale hurt
points: Indian government bonds are likely to face selling pressure in early trades on Friday as a selloff in US Treasuries persists, while traders brace for heavy debt supply of the benchmark paper in the weekly auction later in the day.
The benchmark 6.94 per cent 2036 bond yield is expected to move between 7.23 per cent and 7.28 per cent, according to a private-bank trader, after ending at 7.2467 per cent on Thursday.
New Delhi plans to sell ₹34,000 crore ($3.62 billion) of the benchmark 2036 paper later in the day, taking its outstanding issuance to ₹2.72 lakh crore, the highest for any security ever.

US Treasury yields rose on Thursday after US President Donald Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran, as traders weighed the chance of a larger-than-usual Federal Reserve rate hike next month.
October consumer-price data has beaten forecasts, spurring traders to ramp up bets on a larger rate increase on December 9.

items.title: Four PRTS corridors proposed in Hyderabad; first phase to be completed within a year
points: Multi-level parking facilities have been proposed to facilitate operations on the PRTS corridors.
Representational pic | Photo Credit: The Hindu Chief Minister A.

Revanth Reddy directed officials to complete the tendering process for the proposed Personal Rapid Transit System (PRTS) in Hyderabad by December and ensure that the first phase of the project is completed within a year.

At a review meeting on the proposed PRTS on Thursday, the Chief Minister said the proposed network was aimed at improving connectivity between key government, commercial and public destinations in the city.
One corridor should connect LB Stadium with the Ranigunj bus station via the Ambedkar statue, Indira Park and Lower Tank Bund, he suggested.
Another corridor should connect the Assembly Metro station with Ravindra Bharathi, the Secretariat and IMAX, extending further to Begumpet.
Mr. Revanth Reddy also proposed setting up a multi-level parking facility along Necklace Road, with a dedicated depot for PRTS services as part of the facility.

items.title: Kolkata-Sairang train derailment: Preliminary probe points to faulty braking system
points: Officials and rescuers inspect the derailed coaches of a passenger train near Guwahati, on November 11, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP A preliminary probe into the derailment of the Kolkata-Sairang Express at Digaru Railway Station in Assam on November 11 has…

A six-member probe team, in its report, found that the system primarily responsible for applying brakes in the coaches, technically known as the BP angle cock, was in an isolated condition in the locomotive.

"This may be the reason for this accident, as the brakes may not have been applied when the FP/BP angle cock of the loco was in an isolated condition," a joint note prepared by the probe team on the day of the accident said.
The probe report does not identify who rendered the braking system dysfunctional or whether the train crew overlooked safety procedures to check its functionality before operating the train.

items.title: Meet Colette Kress: The CFO Replacing Nvidia's Jensen Huang
points: Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's Chief Executive Officer (CEO), President, and member of Nvidia's Board of Directors, effective immediately, the company announced.
The Taiwanese-American tech executive has quit the position 33 years after he founded the chipmaker.
The Board has appointed Colette Kress as the Interim CEO of Nvidia, while launching a hunt for the next full-time CEO.
Kress joined Nvidia 13 years ago, in September 2013, as the Executive Vice President and CFO.
Before joining Nvidia, she served as Cisco's Senior Vice President and CFO, Business Technology and Operations Finance, from November 2010 to September 2013.
Kress also served as the Corporate Vice President of Microsoft for about five years, from April 2006 to November 2010.
She earned her Master's in Business Administration (MBA) in Finance from SMU Cox School of Business, graduating in 1996.
Srouji has been associated with Apple for more than 18 years, joining the iPhone maker in March 2008 as the Senior Director, Handheld Chips and VLSI.

points: Cochin Shipyard dividend 2026: Cochin Shipyard shares will remain in focus on Friday, November 13, as today marks as the last opportunity for investors to buy the stock to qualify for its upcoming interim dividend for FY27.
The state-owned shipbuilding company announced an interim dividend of ₹3 per equity share, representing a 60% payout on its face value of ₹5 per share.
Cochin Shipyard said the dividend will be paid to eligible shareholders on or before December 9, 2026.
Cochin Shipyard announced an interim dividend of ₹3 per equity share for FY 2026-27 following its board meeting on November 10, 2026.
Since the Indian stock market follows a T+1 settlement cycle, Friday, November 13, is the last day to purchase Cochin Shipyard shares to qualify for the dividend.
Cochin Shipyard's dividend yield stands at approximately 0.75%, based on its trailing 12-month dividend payout of ₹9 per share and a share price of around ₹1,196.

First off on this list is the Honda 0 Alpha EV.
Now, Honda is getting ready to unveil its production version on December 2, 2026.

Mechanically, the 0 Alpha EV is expected to get two LFP battery pack options ranging between 65 kWh and 75 kWh.
Once launched, it will compete with the Hyundai Creta Electric, Mahindra BE 6 and Maruti Suzuki e Vitara.
Speaking of the powertrain, the India-spec CR-V is expected to get a 2.0-litre four-cylinder petrol engine paired with Honda's two-motor strong hybrid system.

items.title: NITI Aayog praises mobile phone production-linked incentives, says laptop scheme lost time
points: The report, prepared with the Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad, also said the PLI scheme for IT hardware, which covers laptops, tablets, PCs and servers, is still in its early stages, following a failed first version and a redesign that cost…
It brought in ₹20,580 crore of investment and production worth ₹11.61 lakh crore, and created 1.69 lakh jobs, the report said.
The report added that the government paid ₹19,091 crore in incentives, about 56% of the scheme’s ₹34,193 crore outlay, more than half of all PLI money paid across the 14 sectors.
Mobile phone exports rose almost nine-fold, from ₹22,868 crore in FY21 to about ₹2 lakh crore in FY25.
Production under the scheme also fell in 2025-26, the report noted, though it stayed above 50% of the target.
Only four companies have received incentives under the IT hardware scheme so far, totalling ₹98 crore, or 0.57% of its ₹17,000 crore outlay, according to the report.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 8 stocks close above their 200 DMA
points: On November 12, eight Nifty500 stocks that gained over 3% closed above their respective 200-day moving averages (DMA), according to StockEdge’s technical scan data.
The 200-day moving average is a widely tracked technical indicator used to assess a stock’s long-term trend.
When a stock’s price moves above this average, it is generally considered a bullish signal, suggesting a potential improvement in its underlying price momentum.

items.title: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
points: IMF Communications Department Director Julie Kozack. | Photo Credit: AFP India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment and faster creation of high-quality jobs to achieve the medium-term potential growth of 6.8%, the…
In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%.

The upgrade took into account a few factors, including favourable demographics, a large and growing domestic economy or domestic market for goods, and continued momentum on structural reforms, Julie Kozack, Communications Director, IMF, told reporters in…

“But in general, like in many countries, we are encouraging India to take continuing reforms, particularly to focus on how productivity growth can be increased,” she said in response to a question from PTI.
The IMF official said that to further the medium-term potential, India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment, and faster creation of high-quality jobs.
Ms. Kozack said these issues will come up during the Article 4 consultations with India.

items.title: Delhi’s air quality enters ‘severe’ category, AQI breaches 400
points: Delhi’s air quality deteriorated into the “severe” zone — the worst grade on the government’s pollution scale— on Friday morning, with a thick, smoky haze continuing to envelop the Capital.
According to HT’s real-time air quality dashboard and the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 403 at 7.30am, 82 points higher than the previous 24 hours.
Delhi last recorded severe air quality on January 19, when the AQI stood at 410.

HT reported earlier that Delhi’s air quality deteriorated sharply on Thursday, with the city’s PM2.5 concentration more than doubling in 24 hours to 244 micrograms per cubic metre by 6pm — four times the national standard.

The lack of wind limited the dispersion of pollutants, allowing them to accumulate overnight According to HT’s dashboard, 32 of the 59 reporting stations were in the severe category and PM2.5 was the leading pollutant at 48 of the city's 58 monitoring…

items.title: Quad Leaders set to unveil economic security initiatives, strategic infrastructure at Manila Summit
points: Quad member states are expected to unveil several deliverables, mainly focused on economic security and strategic infrastructure, at the leaders’ summit expected to be held on the margins of the Asean Summit in Manila next week, people familiar with the…

The upcoming Quad Leaders’ Summit — the first gathering of the leaders of India, Australia, Japan and the US since September 2024 — is set to be hosted by the US, the people said on condition of anonymity.
India was set to chair the leaders’ summit in 2025, but its efforts to arrange the meeting last year were stymied by lack of clarity on US President Donald Trump’s travel plans.

The deliverables expected to be unveiled at the upcoming summit were finalised at the Quad foreign ministers’ meeting on the margins of the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta on October 31, the people said.

items.title: Warship Hulls To Electronics: India Pushes For Indigenous Naval Systems
points: The Miniratna Defence PSU Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL) has signed a deal with Cyient DLM to set up a joint venture in India to design and manufacture ship electronics, focusing on systems used by Indian Navy warships for navigation, communication,…
Indian yards have been churning out more warships in recent years, but a lot of the high-tech gear inside those hulls remains imported.

According to the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), the partners will work together on navigation and solid-state radars, Electronic Chart Display and Information Systems (ECDIS), autopilots, the Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS), Fleet…
This means more Indian content in HSL's ships and lower dependence on overseas vendors.
R Adm C Raghuram (Retd), HSL Chairman and Managing Director, said the deal would bring more homegrown technology to the ships of the yard.
"The partnership will help India build its technology and manufacturing base in the maritime and defence sectors," said Rajendra Velagapudi, Managing Director and CEO of Cyient DLM.

items.title: National Tribal Literary Festival begins in Delhi; focus on preserving oral traditions
points: The second edition of the National Tribal Literary Festival 2026 began on Thursday in Delhi, bringing together tribal writers, poets, researchers and language experts from across the country to deliberate on preserving indigenous languages, oral traditions…

Organised by the Union ministry of tribal affairs at the India Habitat Centre as part of the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas Pakhwada, the two-day festival is themed “From Oral Tradition to Contemporary Tribal Literature”.

Inaugurating the festival, Union tribal affairs minister Jual Oram stressed the need for systematic documentation of tribal literature, folk songs, folktales and oral traditions, saying the effort must involve not only writers but also lyricists,…
“Preserving tribal languages and oral traditions is central to building Viksit Bharat 2047,” the minister said.
Oral traditions could be documented through other Indian languages, he said, adding that the ministry would collaborate with the Sahitya Akademi and other organisations to promote tribal literature.

items.title: Kia India Sales Breakup Oct 2026 – Seltos, Sonet, Clavis, Sorento, Syros, Carnival
points: Kia India sold 33,462 units in October 2026, up 13.22% from 29,555 units in October 2025 and 4.51% from 32,017 units in September 2026.
The new Seltos crossed the 13,000-unit mark for the first time, while the recently launched Sorento built on its September tally.
The new Seltos led Kia’s lineup with 13,423 units in October, up 88.26% from 7,130 units a year earlier.
The midsize SUV added 830 units month-on-month, the biggest increase in Kia’s lineup, and its share of the company’s sales rose from 39.33% in September to 40.11% in October.
Its share of Kia’s sales fell from 29.65% in September to 26.64% in October.
Seltos, Sonet and the Carens Clavis range together accounted for 87.42% of Kia’s October volumes.
Kia’s made in India flagship SUV, Sorento took fourth place with 2,148 units in October, up 23.52% from 1,739 units in September, its launch month.

items.title: Delhi education department asks task force to submit recommendations on fixing dropouts, low attendance by November 15
points: The education department constituted a 26-member panel on August 17 under the Samagra Shiksha Society to comprehensively examine the challenges related to dropout rates, learning outcomes, and the impact of low student attendance on the Mid-Day Meal…

According to the minutes of the meeting held on September 9, the committee decided that the Delhi State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT) would identify 10 schools in each district grappling with these issues and conduct an in-depth…

“Based on the analysis undertaken by SCERT, the Task Force shall recommend practical, feasible, and suggestive interventions at the school, district, and headquarters levels for improving attendance, reducing dropout rates, and enhancing student engagement.
The recommendations shall be submitted by November 15, 2026,” one of the 18 decisions taken by the committee, according to the minutes of the meeting accessed by HT.
The committee also decided that the impact of seasonal migrations, family movement, pollution-related restrictions, and other external factors on attendance should be studied through data.

It is aiming to release the final guidelines in the first half of 2027, according to an official familiar with the development.

items.title: Tripura Minor Girl Rescued From Suspected Human Trafficking Network
points: A minor girl from Agartala, who was allegedly lured to Bengaluru with the promise of a film audition, has been rescued and safely brought back to Tripura with the help of her father, social activists and members of a social organisation.
The girl, who went missing on October 13, was allegedly persuaded by a woman, identified by her as Nishima Ben, to travel to Bengaluru for a film audition.
While speaking to ANI, recalling her ordeal, the girl said, "Nishima Ben told me that a film was being shot in Bengaluru and that auditions were being held there.
Following this, Yuvraj Chowdhury took my gold chain as a pledge and gave me Rs 30,000.
She also alleged that repeated demands for money were made to her family, with the amounts reportedly changing from Rs 5 lakh to Rs 8 lakh and subsequently Rs 2 lakh.

items.title: Twin cyclone leave livelihoods in tatters
points: Published - November 13, 2026 07:39 am IST - Perupalem/Narsapur A farmer showing the damaged paddy crop following Cyclone Arnab at Tadepalli mandal in Guntur district. | Photo Credit: G.N.
RAO For generations, coconut trees have been more than just crops for the people in the coastal districts of Dr. B.R.
Konaseema district has witnessed the swath of destruction, with over 73,500 coconut trees uprooted and paddy destroyed across 1,18,109 acres, leaving around 88,000 farmers in tatters.
Meanwhile, in West Godavari district, 27,397 coconut trees were destroyed, affecting more than 5,000 small and marginal growers.
Andhra Pradesh was ravaged by two cyclones between October 28 and November 3.

One was a ‘Very Severe’ Cyclonic Storm (VSCS) Arnab and the other, a ‘Severe’ Cyclonic Storm (SCS) Murasu, leaving the districts of West Godavari, Konaseema, and Bapatla in ruins, while Guntur, East Godavari and Palnadu were also affected, according to the…

items.title: Passing out parade of over 2,700 Agniveers at INS Chilka today
points: More than 2,700 Navy Agniveers will complete their 16-week ab-initio training and pass out of the INS Chilka training facility in Odisha today, officials said.
More than 600 regular Naviks of the Coast Guard will also complete their training alongside the Navy Agniveers.
Navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan will be the chief guest and reviewing officer of the passing out parade in Chilka.
The latest batches of Army and Indian Air Force Agniveers will pass out of their training establishments in December.
The new framework was cleared by the Cabinet and unveiled by Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani on November 4.

The Agnipath reboot was announced by Subramani weeks before the three services were set to release 75% of Agniveers from their first batch after four years of service, retaining only the 25% selected on merit for another 15 years under the scheme’s earlier…

items.title: Your roots may be in villages, but your flight has no limits: President Droupadi Murmu
points: President Droupadi Murmu on Thursday urged students from Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) to dream big and pursue their ambitions with dedication, discipline and self-confidence, saying their rural backgrounds should never limit their aspirations.
“Your roots are connected to your villages, but there is no limit to your flight,” Murmu told a gathering of meritorious tribal students during an interaction at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
The President emphasised that education should not remain merely a means of earning a livelihood, but should also equip young people to create employment opportunities for others.
The interaction was organised by the ministry of tribal affairs as part of Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada, observed annually to mark the birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Bhagwan Birsa Munda.

Highlighting the importance of tribal education in achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, Murmu said the development of every region and every section of society was essential for the country’s progress.

items.title: High risk, low pay: J&K’s SPOs living on the edge
points: Despite handling frontline counter-insurgency operations, routine law-and-order duties, and even serving as orderlies at senior officers’ residences, special police officers (SPOs) in Jammu and Kashmir take home a meagre monthly honorarium ranging from…

The killing of two missing SPOs—Rashpal Kumar, 45, and Babbi Chand, 57—in the upper reaches of Dachhan has once again brought the precarious working conditions of these auxiliary personnel into focus.
Yet, the government still pays a fixed, low honorarium based strictly on years of service.” Currently, SPOs with less than five years of service earn ₹6,000 a month.
In March 2022, the Union ministry of home affairs (MHA) approved a revised scheme replacing the old VDCs with newly structured village defence groups (VDGs).

While intended to revive dormant village defence networks and streamline direct payments, the policy triggered widespread resentment by capping the monthly honorarium for all VDG members—including veteran SPOs—at a flat ₹4,500.
How could someone like me accept ₹4,500 a month?” Kumar asks.

points: Here is a list of 3 such new twin-cylinder motorcycles that Royal Enfield will be launching in the market soon.
Royal Enfield will officially launch the Himalayan 750 motorcycle at the 2026 Motoverse in Goa.
The Himalayan 750 is Royal Enfield’s biggest Himalayan to date.
The motorcycle will be offered with a 743cc, twin-cylinder, air-oil-cooled, parallel-twin engine that generates 55 PS and 63 Nm of peak torque.

items.title: Amidst simmering tensions, India-Bangladesh consular dialogue postponed
points: The source indicated that the postponement of the dialogue was mainly on account of growing tensions in the bilateral relationship caused by Ms. Hasina’s announcement that she will return to Bangladesh next month.
The planned consular dialogue would have been the first such meeting between the two sides in more than two years.
The last such dialogue was held in New Delhi on May 29, 2024, just over two months before the Hasina government fell in a youth-led uprising in Dhaka.
The consular dialogue was scheduled to be held in Dhaka at the level of Director Generals of the Foreign Ministries of both countries.
The number of Indian visas issued was drastically reduced when tensions broke out in August 2024.

According to sources, India has gradually increased the number of visas issued to travellers from Bangladesh in recent months, especially after the election of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in February this year.

points: After his extradition from Oman, the CBI had arrested Chandrakar and was granted his custody by the same court last week.

After the expiry of his custodial remand, the CBI produced him in court.

Mr. Giri informed that while CBI did not ask for any further extension of his client’s custody, the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) that is probing the money laundering angle also filed an application seeking execution of a non-bailable warrant against…

In 2024, cases related to the alleged Mahadev app scam were handed over to the CBI, while the ED has been probing the money laundering linked to the cases.

items.title: 57th IFFI to be held in Goa from Nov 20, adopts ‘Stories Without Borders’ theme
points: The 57th edition of the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) will be held in Goa from November 20 to 28.
The festival will follow the theme “Stories Without Borders”, highlighting cinema’s ability to connect audiences across cultures and geographies.
The festival’s highlights, key programmes and major attractions will be unveiled at a curtain-raiser press conference in Goa on Friday.

Goa chief minister Pramod Sawant will attend the event along with secretary to the Union ministry of information and broadcasting Chanchal Kumar and chairperson of the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) G Krishnakumar.
Filmmaker Ashutosh Gowariker, who is the festival director for the 2026 edition, will also be present.

IFFI is one of the country’s major international film festivals which provides a platform for filmmakers from India and abroad to showcase their work and promote an understanding of different cultures through cinema.
The 2026 edition is expected to feature a diverse selection of Indian and international films, reflecting the festival’s expanding global participation.

items.title: Let Abhishek Banerjee submit a list of judges who belong to the BJP: Calcutta high court
points: The Calcutta high court on Thursday observed that Mamata All India Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee should submit a list of judges who favour the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and those supporting the All India Trinamool Congress.
This comes days after the Diamond Harbour MP attacked the judiciary for dilly-dallying over a case related to his security downgrade after the BJP government came to power.
Let your client give the list of those who belong to the BJP and those who belong to the AITC,” a bench of Justice Krishna Rao remarked.
On November 7, Abhishek Banerjee reportedly said that a case he filed over his security downgrade had been only “partly heard”, alleging that the “BJP had exerted pressure”.
The matter was to be heard again on (October) 13.
The additional advocate general told the high court that Abhishek Banerjee's remarks constitute criminal contempt.
“This has no connection with the petition,” senior advocate Shoeb Alam, representing Banerjee in the petition related to security, argued before the court.

points: The Ernakulam District Crime Branch arrested Rajendran Vellapalath, chairman of the Kerala Pravasi Association, on Thursday for his alleged involvement in forging documents purportedly issued in the name of the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to extort money…
He was arrested at Nedumbassery after he allegedly contacted the Indian Credit Cooperative Society in Thrissur, offering to settle an issue after the firm received a forged ED notice.

Scientists pointed out that textile dyeing activities generate coloured wastewater containing dyes, salts and organic contaminants.
To address this challenge, CSIR-IICT developed the decentralised treatment system specifically for rural and semi-urban textile clusters.
Calling it a true “Lab to Loom” initiative, CSIR-IICT Director D.
Srinivasa Reddy said that the project translates indigenous research into a practical and sustainable solution for the handloom sector.

Nakrekal MLA Vemula Veeresham said that the facility would help protect local water resources, support the livelihoods of handloom artisans and also help showcase the village’s rich handloom heritage.

items.title: Voluntary transferof priority ration cards allowed till December 8
points: The Civil Supplies department has announced that individuals holding priority ration cards (Yellow and Pink cards) despite being ineligible can voluntarily transfer them to the general category without facing fines or legal action until December 8.

According to officials, strict inspections will follow the deadline, and those found holding priority cards unlawfully will be penalised with the market price of all subsidised food grains received to date.

items.title: Priyanka Gandhi pays tribute to Cheruvayal Raman, visits family in Wayanad
points: Ms. Vadra, who is on a three-day visit to the Wayanad constituency, spent time with Raman’s family at their residence and enquired about their well-being.
Speaking to reporters after the visit, Vadra described Raman as “a really good man and a special soul”, saying that his passing had left her deeply saddened.

Recalling one of their conversations, Ms. Vadra said Raman had told her that the numerous awards and honours he had received meant little to him unless they translated into meaningful benefits for his community.
Following Raman’s death on October 14, Ms. Vadra had also paid tribute to him through a post on X, recalling the affectionate bond they shared.
Born on June 6, 1952, Raman belonged to the Kurichya tribal community and emerged as one of the most distinguished custodians of Kerala’s traditional agricultural heritage.
He began concentrating on farming at the age of 10, developing an abiding commitment to agriculture that eventually became the defining purpose of his life.

items.title: RTI Act strengthens people’s voice in democracy, says Keralam Information Commissioner
points: Ramakrishnan said here on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
He was inaugurating a seminar on ‘Everything you need to know about the right to information’ at the Municipal Town Hall here.
Mr. Ramakrishnan said the Supreme Court had, through several judgments, recognised the right to information as part of the fundamental right even before the RTI Act came into force.
He traced the origins of the law to the people’s movement led by farmers and workers in Devdungri village in Rajasthan.
The campaign led by Aruna Roy and the efforts of organisations such as the National Campaign for People’s Right to Information helped build support for the legislation.
Following these movements, Parliament passed the RTI Act in 2005.
He also clarified that the 30-day period allowed for providing information should not be treated as a mandatory waiting period.
Around 800 officials from various government departments attended the seminar.

items.title: 91 days since Parliament adjourned, session delay puzzles Opposition on Centre’s motives
points: The Union government is yet to announce the next session of Parliament or prorogue the monsoon session, leaving the Opposition and other parties guessing even as 91 days have passed since the Houses were adjourned sine die on August 13.
The delay has fuelled speculation that the Centre may extend the monsoon session by a few days to push through the Delimitation Bill and the Constitution Amendment Bill.
With 12 days already gone in November, the government is running short of time if it wants to convene a fresh winter session.
According to people aware of the details, the Union government is also keen to push ahead with its plan to pass the 131st Constitution Amendment Bill.
The bills are a prerequisite for rolling out 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state assemblies.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will also preside over a meeting of the Council of Ministers scheduled for November 18.

items.title: PM Modi greets overseas Congress chief Pitroda with ‘happy Diwali’ after warm remarks
points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday exchanged Diwali greetings with Indian Overseas Congress chief Sam Pitroda after the latter praised him as a person, describing him as a warm and caring friend and appreciating his oratory and hard work.
“Happy Diwali and Nutan Varsh Abhinandan to you Sam Bhai and to Anjana Ben.
The Gujarati New Year begins on November 10.
A close associate of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, Pitroda was one of the principal architects and key technical leaders of India’s telecom revolution in the 1980s.
Pitroda’s remarks come amid intensified protests by the Congress-led Opposition against the government, with parties demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.
“Indian Overseas Congress Chairman Sam Pitroda has stated that he shares a good personal relationship with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and has visited his home in Gujarat several times.
In May 2019, during the Lok Sabha election campaign, he was asked about allegations concerning the Congress leadership’s role in the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.

India makes gains against TB, deaths down 38% since 2015: Centre
points: India's estimated TB deaths declined by 38% between 2015 and 2025, signaling significant progress in controlling the disease.
The treatment success rate for drug-susceptible TB reached 94%, supported by innovative diagnostic methods and comprehensive patient care.
The ongoing TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan effectively identified nearly 15 lakh asymptomatic TB cases throughout the campaign.
Despite progress, drug-resistant TB remains a challenge, with a notable treatment gap.
